messages:
matt: FYI we're seeing a customer P99 tail regression starting ~02:00 UTC for short prompts (~10-20 tokens). p95 slipped from 120ms to ~420ms, p99 to ~1.8s. Dashboard: /d/redwood/batcher-latency?org=redwood

devon: saw alerts. traces show a bunch of requests stuck in the continuous-batcher pending queue for ~700-900ms before dispatch. CPU/GPU utilization normal.

sara: any recent config rolls on the batcher?

matt: rolled a batcher tuning change last night to increase max_batch_tokens from 8192 -> 16384 and reduced linger_ms from 8 -> 2 to lower avg latency for long seqs. hypothesis: for tiny prompts at high QPS, the smaller linger_ms means we open more micro-batches but token cap now groups cross-tenant bursts oddly, causing queue headlock.

devon: interesting — the token cap interacts with greedy coalesce. When linger_ms small, we send quickly, but the runtime's batching kernel waits for token budget aggregation and ends up serializing a lot of tiny requests into many tiny kernel calls. That increases scheduling jitter and tail.

anya-support: customer reported retries and 502s too. Support saw spikes in request_timeouts from client side during the window. Request IDs: r-12a4.., r-12a8... attached in ticket.

matt: repro command I used locally: 
```
./replay_load --pattern short_prompts.json --qps 600 --concurrency 400 --duration 8m --tenant acme-test
```
I attached a sample replay payload to the ticket. Repro reliably produces p99 ~1.6s on latest canary.

sara: can you paste the current continuous-batcher config from canary?

matt: config snippet: 
```
batcher:
  mode: continuous
  linger_ms: 2
  max_batch_tokens: 16384
  max_batch_size: 128
  min_coalesce_qps: 50
  token_budget_window_ms: 40
```

devon: two immediate mitigation options: 1) revert max_batch_tokens to 8192 (less aggressive aggregation), or 2) temporarily increase linger_ms to 6-8ms just for the tiny-prompt route (route-based override) so coalesce has time without increasing avg latency for long prompts.

anya-support: customer wants ETA — can we do a fast fix? They are seeing intermittent timeouts.

sara: ops-bot can we patch a canary with route override: for route /v1/generate-short set linger_ms: 8 and max_batch_size: 64, leave global unchanged. Also enable extra logging to capture per-batch token counts.

ops-bot: acknowledged. Creating canary build and deploying to 2 nodes in us-west-2. Will post once up.

matt: rolling the canary now to two nodes (svc/batchers-canary). If p99 improves in 15m we can push hotfix.

(devon shares quick analysis): logs show the pathological tail occurs when a large multi-token request triggers token-budget refill and steals GPU kernel slots, delaying 100s of tiny requests queued on the same worker. It's a scheduling contention pattern, not pure CPU/GPU saturation.

ops-bot: canary deployed at 1755552600. Extra batch logs enabled.

matt: initial canary numbers: p95 down to 140ms, p99 down to 320ms on canary nodes for the replay. Good signal.

sara: recommend: 1) hotpatch route-level linger_ms=6 and max_batch_tokens=8192 for production, 2) follow-up: implement a token-budget fairness gate so tiny requests aren't delayed by large token allocations, 3) add a dashboard split by request token count.

anya-support: I'll update the customer with ETA ~30-45m and note we're rolling a mitigation.

matt: proceeding with hotpatch. Will monitor closely and prepare rollback playbook (revert to previous global values) if we see regressions.

sara: thanks team. After stabilization we should add an automated canary test for short-prompts at high QPS in CI to catch this config interaction earlier.

anya-support: customer ack'd the update and will monitor their side.

ops-bot: hotpatch rolled to prod at 1755552725 on all nodes. Monitoring windows: 30m.

matt: post-hotpatch summary (interim): p95 ~130-160ms, p99 ~300-400ms, no client timeouts observed in last 10m. Closing loop with customer now.
